chapter_title: Concerning the Sect of the Basket
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

## ¶5

The [GAP-1] and the great [GAP-2] and the great Divine Intellectual Principle that is [GAP-3] — this first regenerating state of the will that is with the [GAP-4] — thirty-six divine influxes constituting a fullness of spiritual operation [GAP-5] twenty-two divine influxes corresponding to every mode through which divine truth can be expressed [GAP-6] but [GAP-7] of the twenty-two modes of divine expression [GAP-8] — the seven holy foundational principles that sust[GAP-9: ain] — the encompassing natural cognition that bounds the whole spiritual form of the human [GAP-10] — four operative truths that are distributed to the [GAP-11] whole spiritual constitution, upholding the divine power [GAP-12] in the external and lowest degree, which is the natural foundation upon which all interior states of wisdom rest [GAP-13] — these other five divine faculties, the qualities proceeding from the Divine Human, they that [GAP-14] the whole spiritual constitution is established and made firm [GAP-15] — the divine calling forth and the will's answering reception [GAP-16] — the radiance of divine wisdom from the [GAP-17] — the Indestructible Truth proceeding from Divine Good [GAP-18] — they have become opposing falsities and hostile evils [GAP-19] — they lead and govern it.

---

## ¶6

The third degree also, [GAP-20] in the external and lowest plane, there are twelve complete principles of faith standing firm there. However, the full number of the twelve representative forms of spiritual truth [GAP-21] — the three fundamental supporting principles of divine power that [GAP-22] — foundational truths upholding the plane of conscious awareness [GAP-23] — the other three [GAP-24] — they are the external truths clothing interior goods, which the Divine Proceeding that orders all spiritual life [GAP-25] — He disposed them in that state of the mind's formation [GAP-26] — that cast them forth, together with [GAP-27] — which is manifested therein [GAP-28] — this [GAP-29] — brought to completeness before [GAP-30] — the great Guardian Principle governing passage between interior and exterior states [GAP-31] — within his governing power [GAP-32] — these are the three great [GAP-33] — against [GAP-34] — are in the midst of human minds [GAP-35] — perceives and acknowledges [GAP-36] — commits his inmost life to their keeping [GAP-37].

---

### Translator's Note

The spiritual architecture here describes how the Lord's influx sustains the regenerating human through three discrete degrees: the celestial (the Divine Mind and the Youth-will), the spiritual (the seven holy pillars and the five faculties from the Divine Human), and the natural (the twelve principles of faith and the three supporting truths). The "sea surrounding the universe" is the body of natural memory-knowledge that encloses and bounds the whole spiritual organism. The "Adamant of Light" — indestructible truth from divine good — stands as the principle that cannot be shattered even when surrounding states become hostile. The "great Porter" is the guardian truth that governs what may pass between the external and the internal human. The passage culminates in a doctrine of trust: whoever perceives these ordered principles and commits his inmost life to their governance is sustained by the whole divine arrangement.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: The [Light] and the great [Power] and the great Mind that is [in] this Youth that is with the [Maiden of Light, and the] thirty-six angels [and the] twenty-two angels [that are with him] but [the number] of the twenty-two [is] the seven pillars that stan[d in] the sea that surrounds the universe [and the] four angels that are distributed to the [whole] universe, supporting the mightiness [from] below, which is the earth of all the heavens [and also] these other five gods, the sons of the Man, they that [through them] the universe is stood firm [together with] the summons and the obedience [and] the splendour of the [Light] the Adamant of Light [against those that] they are become enemies [yet] they guide it.

The third also, [that is] below, there are twelve powers standing firm there. However, the number of the twelve images [and also] the three great pillars of mightiness that [are the] pillars supporting the disk [and] the other three [powers] they are the garments that the Living Spirit [wore] he put them at that time [upon those] that threw them, together with [the light] which is displayed therein [and] this [that is made] perfect before [the] great Porter [who is] in his power [and] these are the three great [powers] against [those that] are in the midst of people [and whoever] knows [them and] entrusts his soul to them [shall be saved].

fills.explanation: In Manichaean cosmological enumeration, "the Light" is the fundamental divine attribute that naturally opens a triad, corresponding to divine good in Swedenborgian terms; it stands without the modifier "great" as the primary principle.
Power completes the classic Manichaean triad Light-Power-Mind, corresponding to divine capacity/omnipotence that mediates between the good (Light) and the understanding (Mind).
The divine intellectual principle (great Mind/Nous) resides within the Youth (Third Messenger), corresponding to understanding dwelling within the regenerating will.
In Manichaean cosmology the Youth (Third Messenger) is always paired with the Maiden of Light as his operative counterpart; the conjunction introduces the subsequent enumeration of angel groups.
Simple conjunction connecting two enumerated groups of angels (thirty-six and twenty-two), standard Kephalaia listing syntax.
Common Kephalaia construction describing angelic attendants; the twenty-two angels attend the Youth, completing the clause before the enumerative breakdown introduced by "but."
Parallels the identical construction in ¶6 ("the number of the twelve images"), introducing an enumerative breakdown of the twenty-two into constituent groups.
Completes the predicate identifying what the number of the twenty-two consists of: the seven pillars, the four angels, and other cosmic structures.
Completes "stand in" — the seven cosmic pillars stand in the surrounding sea, a standard Manichaean cosmological image of foundational structures within the cosmic ocean.
Simple conjunction introducing the next element in the cosmic enumeration — the four corner-angels distributed throughout the universe.
The spiritual reading specifies "whole spiritual constitution"; in the Kephalaia's natural register, the four angels are distributed to the whole universe, upholding it from every direction.
The four corner-angels support the cosmic power from below, corresponding to the spiritual reading's "in the external and lowest degree" — they uphold from the lowest plane.
Transitional conjunction adding the five sons of the Man to the cosmic enumeration, continuing the list of supporting cosmic entities.
Standard Coptic resumptive relative construction: "they that through them the universe is stood firm" = "they through whom the universe is established," describing the five sons as cosmic supports.
Introduces additional cosmic entities (Call and Answer) alongside the five sons, indicating they belong to the same divine assembly that upholds the universe.
Simple conjunction continuing the enumeration of cosmic entities: the Call/Answer, then the Splendour, then the Adamant.
"The splendour of the Light" is a standard Manichaean title corresponding to the Keeper of Splendour (one of the five sons), expressing the radiance of divine wisdom proceeding from divine good.
The Adamant of Light (Adamas, a warrior-son of the Living Spirit) is set against the archons who became enemies of the light, corresponding to indestructible truth opposing falsities.

Introduces the paradox that the archonic enemies, though hostile, still serve a governing function in the cosmic order — corresponding to Swedenborg's principle that even evil spirits serve the divine economy.
Identifies the third cosmic level as the one situated below, corresponding to the natural/external degree in Swedenborgian discrete degrees.
Connects the twelve images to the three great pillars in an enumerative breakdown, paralleling the structure of ¶5 where cosmic elements are listed additively.
Identifies the three great pillars of mightiness as the specific pillars supporting the cosmic disk, equating the title with the function.
Simple conjunction introducing the complementary group — "the other three" — which pairs with the three pillars to account for six of the twelve powers.

Generic Kephalaia term naming the other three cosmic entities before their specific identification as "garments" of the Living Spirit; "powers" is the most common unspecified divine-entity term in the Kephalaia register.

In Manichaean cosmogony the Living Spirit wore divine garments (his sons as armor) when descending to create; the garments clothe interior goods, corresponding to external truths covering divine realities.
The Living Spirit placed his garments upon the defeated archons, subduing and binding them into the cosmic structure — corresponding to divine truths being imposed upon hostile natural states.

The archons were thrown down together with the trapped light particles, which are then manifested/displayed within the cosmic structures — a core Manichaean teaching about the light mixed into matter.
Simple conjunction connecting the clause about the light displayed within the cosmic structures to the subsequent description of the form made perfect before the Porter.

Completes "this that is made perfect before the great Porter" — the cosmic form is brought to completeness under the governance of the guardian principle, matching the spiritual reading's "brought to completeness."
Supplies the definite article before "great Porter," the standard Kephalaia title for Atlas/Omophoros who governs passage between interior and exterior cosmic states.
Relative clause connecting the Porter to his governing power, describing the guardian principle as residing within his sphere of authority.
Transitional conjunction bridging the description of the Porter's power to the summary statement identifying the three great powers.
Summarizes the three cosmic entities as "powers" — a standard generic Kephalaia term for divine operative principles that protect against hostile forces among humanity.
Introduces the hostile entities that the three great powers oppose — the evil forces active among human beings, corresponding to falsities and evils within the natural mind.
Introduces the concluding wisdom saying in standard Manichaean didactic form: "whoever knows... and entrusts..." — the one who perceives the divine order and commits to it receives salvation.
Provides the object of knowing and the conjunction: "whoever knows them and entrusts his soul" — perceiving the three powers and then committing one's life to their governance.

Standard Manichaean salvific conclusion to a wisdom saying: whoever perceives the divine cosmic order and commits his inmost life to it shall be saved — the natural-register expression of spiritual regeneration's promise.
